action: Review exposure, access controls and monitoring for activity that alters business records or approval processes, as CERT-In advises; the advisory itself was not read, so check cert-in.org.in for its full recommendations.
date_note: The advisory is described only as 'recent' and is not dated in the article; the date is the IANS article's own date.
exec: CERT-In says payment fraud can pass normal approval checks without any attack on payment APIs, and that it now reaches government-linked payment providers.
plain: India's cyber agency warns that criminals use AI tools to change how businesses approve payments, so fraudulent transfers look legitimate. It says banks are not the only targets.

sources.name: Telangana Today (IANS): CERT-In warns of AI-driven cyberattacks targeting business payment systems

summary: According to an IANS report, a recent CERT-In advisory says cybercriminals use AI-powered tools to manipulate business payment workflows and carry out unauthorised transactions. CERT-In says attacks now reach technology service providers supporting government-linked payment processes and platforms handling vendor or partner payouts, not only banks. It says the concern is not limited to payment API security, because a transaction may pass the usual application and approval checks.
title: CERT-In warns AI-powered tools are used to manipulate business payment workflows, IANS reports

validation.note: One publisher (IANS via Telangana Today) read; Moneycontrol's article on the same advisory would not load; the CERT-In advisory itself was not read.
